newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MMI/Alpic in India health insurance deal.
newsitem.headline: MMI/Alpic in India health insurance deal.

text.p: Insurance group, MMI Ltd and its German major shareholder, Allianz AG, said on Tuesday they had signed a deal with Indian finance group, Alpic Finance Ltd, with a view to entering the Indian health insurance market.
MMI said the agreement followed the recent announcement by the former Indian Finance Minister that the government intends to privatise health insurance.

Earlier this month, joint venture discussions between Alpic and Australian insurance group FAI Insurances Ltd were ended with FAI saying it would open its own representative office in India at the appropriate time.
Alpic has a banking licence in India, and will start its banking activities in 1998.
"The proposed Allianz-MMI-Alpic joint venture intends to enter the general and life insurance markets in India when these are liberalised," MMI said in a statement.

MMI's general Manager International, Angus Maciver told Reuters the term health insurance in India referred to personal accident and illness cover and could include areas such as workers compensation.

"The joint venture plans to develop products that will cover a wide cross-section of the Indian community. These will not be limited to higher-income families or to the metropolitan areas," the company said.
The proposed venture in India is MMI's third initiative since late 1995.
MMI announced its participation in reinsurance business in Singapore in late 1996 and in March 1997, commenced its business insurance operations in Guam and Saipan.
Allianz owns about 38 percent of MMI.
